Inside the Fern website design

Fern is a developer tools website built with custom code, Next.js, Astro, and Tailwind CSS. Its pages are built from navbar, stats, features, testimonials, CTA, other, hero, editorial, and footer sections, shown here in full-page captures and a scroll recording. Typography: GT Planar (display text, headings, and body text) and JetBrains Mono (monospaced text). Colours: background #F7F7F7, text #202020, surface #FFFFFF, secondary text #737373.

Start with OpenAPI. Generate SDKs in multiple languages, interactive API documentation, and an agent-first CLI. Its visual style is minimal, corporate, and developer focused, with navigation bar, hero, and logo strip among its components.

WHY WE PICKED IT

A deep blue hero with a soft gradient horizon frames an actual docs browser and a mono-type terminal window side by side, showing the product mid-task instead of describing it. Below, a plain grey background with bold black stat numbers and small logo marks keeps the long page easy to scan while still building trust through named customers.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR
Navbar: a short menu: only the destinations visitors actually look for
Stats: three or four numbers that matter to the buyer
Features: benefits framed around what the user gets, not internal capability names
Testimonials: names, roles, and photos or logos for credibility
